searchText: some 7702 questions is transaction with empty `authorization_list` valid? is setting the code rolled back if transaction fails? I guess set code transaction can also be creation transaction with empty `destination`. What happens if both the `authorization_list` and initcode execution result set code of the same address, I guess initcode wins? empty list is valid and setting code is not rolled back if the tx reverts. should probably just ban creation txs via 7702 If setting code is permanent perhaps just ban all calls not just creation transactions. The next TX will get it. It does close a one-time mev-proof window however. sorry not sure i understand this? Banning creation transactions to prevent some corner case because of them reverting or address collision won't cover all the cases. The same collisionons can happen by calling create in a normal tx call, or have the normal call revert for any number of reasons. I don't understand why create transactions create a different issue. I don't think create transactions cause an issue per se, I just think there is no need for create so we should make `destination` required like 4844 and keep it simple It's better to ban and relax then to allow and ban, but I think there are useful cases where a contract creation could depend on a proxy being set (or a creation of a contract based on a blob being present, such as genesis of an L2). But the practicality of banning for ease of testing is compelling.
